items.title: Randy Sandke interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 10, 1997
items.q: people like Kenny Davern, Warren Vache, Scott Hamilton, to me they’re very personal voices

ctx.x: And if you go a little above their heads, they’ll just say things like, “oooh, that went right through my head” or something. I hear these little bits and pieces.

Yeah. And I mean that brings up another kind of interesting facet is this whole idea, which I’ve really had to face, of playing older styles which are really basically formed. Like these styles are set, but to try to play it, I mean like here is, okay I have this career, this is what I do. Is it possible to do it in a creative way and in a personal way? And I have come to the belief that yes it is. I don’t mean to hold myself as a great example, but people like Kenny Davern, Warren Vache, Scott Hamilton, to me…

Well you’ve certainly played with a long list of the really established veterans, and they seem to embrace your approach. The World’s Greatest Jazz Band and Benny Carter. Is there a group of people that you really, really look forward to playing with?
